Hi Jane — thanks for the worksheet and the clear SLOs. We've reviewed the sheet and I attached our filled answers (redwood_dedicated_rfi_answers_v1.xlsx). Summary below to get the conversation started:

- Recommended GPU mix (initial): A100-80GB x majority for throughput-heavy batch generation and longer contexts; H100 for low-latency single-turn chat where p95 <= 120ms is tight; L4 / T4 class for dense embedding workloads and low-cost inference.
- Baseline guidance (example profile): 200 concurrent chat sessions (interactive, avg 60 tokens per turn) => estimate ~2.5M tokens/day. For this profile we show a conservative commit of 4 A100-80GB seats with a 20% burst lane to handle diurnal peaks.
- Packing & batching: Redwood's runtime does continuous batching with per-tenant prefix caching and token-level KV reuse; packing granularity and batch window are configurable per-pool to trade latency vs throughput. We recommend a narrow batch window (2–4 ms) for strict p95 targets plus optimized kernel selection (FP16/AMP + selective quantization) for the chat model.
- Burst model: Reserved pools can be configured with an attached burst (shared) lane. Burst usage is billed at a premium rate if it exceeds reserved commit; we can separate burst SLAs if you want predictable cold tails.
- Commitment term: 12-month minimum on Dedicated commitments; 3-month pilots available with prorated conversion into a 12-month contract.
- Security: Dedicated pools are provisioned in your VPC with optional customer-managed KMS keys and audit log export.

Follow-ups I need from your side:
1) Workload mix (percentage chat vs embeddings vs reranking).
2) Expected peak tail factor (ratio of peak qps to 90 day avg).
3) Any hard constraints on preemptible hardware in the pool.

I'll loop in Markus and Dev to confirm packing assumptions and to produce a small exportable CSV sizing model.

Monica — quick tech check. The packing factor of 0.82 is reasonable for mixed chat workloads if we reserve a small tail slot for hot KV cache warmups. Throughput estimates (conservative):
- A100-80GB (mixed-precision FP16, tuned kernels): ~350–450k tokens/sec of sustained batching throughput for generative workloads at 2k context average per batch when using contiguous packing. Per-GPU interactive token throughput (low latency, narrow batch window): ~40–65k tokens/sec depending on model.
- H100 (optimized for low-latency steering): similar peak throughput, better single-request latency; use for the p95-sensitive min-latency pool.
- L4: ~120–200k tokens/sec for dense embedding scoring with smaller memory footprint.

Suggested sizing for Procura sample profile (200 concurrent sessions, avg 60 tokens/turn, 2 turns):
- Baseline commit: 6x A100-80GB (covers steady-state with room for model growth and larger context).
- Tail / low-latency pool: 2x H100 configured with <3 ms batch window and pre-warmed KV caches.
- Burst policy: attach shared burst lane with a 30% premium billing; suggest a hard cap at 2x additional A100-equivalent units to control cost.

If Finance pushes back on 6x baseline we can offer a phased approach: 3x A100 + 1x H100 for pilot (3 months), convert to 6x after acceptance. I'll prepare a CSV model with the above numbers.

— Markus
